extracted.intended_audience: PD/PIs and institutional staff preparing NIH resubmission (A1) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and procedural requirements for preparing and submitting a resubmission (A1) to NIH following an unfunded competing new, renewal, or revision application (A0). Covers eligibility, timing, required materials, submission methods, and format constraints for resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmission is an unfunded application that has been modified following initial review and resubmitted for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A resubmission application can follow a competing new, renewal, or revision application (A0) that was not selected for funding (including applications 'not discussed' in review). A resubmission has a suffix in its application identification number, e.g., A1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent application types eligible for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions may follow a competing new, renewal, or revision application (A0) that was not selected for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes applications that were 'not discussed' in review. Resubmissions were previously called 'amended' applications (hence 'A1').

rubrics_metrics.name: Single resubmission limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a single resubmission (A1) of a competing new, renewal, or revision application (A0) will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After an unsuccessful resubmission (A1), you may submit the idea as a new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding opportunity must allow resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission must be listed in the Application Types Allowed section of the funding opportunity in order to submit a resubmission application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may resubmit using a different PA, PAR, or PAS program announcement that accepts resubmissions, provided eligibility and other requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a new application (not a resubmission) is required
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a new application (not a resubmission) if switching between a program announcement and request for application (RFA) or if changing activity codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NOT-OD-18-197 for exceptions. You may submit an unfunded application as new again, without a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for submitting a resubmission (37 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit the resubmission application within 37 months of the new, renewal, or revision application it follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thereafter, the application must be submitted as a new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of summary statement required before resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a resubmission application can be submitted, the PD/PI must have received the summary statement from the previous review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss questions about resubmission with the NIH Institute/Center scientific contact associated with your grant application as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and form selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission applications must be submitted through Grants.gov to NIH using one of the Submission Options: ASSIST, Workspace, or an institutional system-to-system solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 'Resubmission' in Type of Application field (box 8) on the SF424 R&R form. You may include a cover letter, though not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction requirement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: You must include an introduction that: summarizes substantial additions, deletions, and changes to the application; responds to the issues and criticism raised in the summary statement; and does not markup changes within application attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The introduction is one page or less in length, unless specified otherwise in the funding opportunity or on the table of page limits. In a multi-project application, you must submit an introduction with the Overall component, but introductions within the other components are optional. In a resubmission of a revision application the same introduction must describe within the standard page limit the nature and impact of the revision and summarize the changes made to the application since the last submission. Do not highlight, color, bold or italicize changes in Research Strategy or other attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting/markup anti-patterns for revised attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not markup changes within application attachments (e.g., do not highlight, color, bold or italicize changes in Research Strategy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking up changes is not allowed; summarize changes in the introduction instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations about extent of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: You may need to make significant changes to the resubmission, compared to the new application that it follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond directly to criticisms in the summary statement and make substantive modifications as needed to address reviewer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on duplicate or highly overlapping applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH will not accept duplicate or highly overlapping applications under review at the same time, except in certain limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposed submissions are sufficiently distinct in scope/aims to avoid simultaneous overlapping review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development and fellowship reference letter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Career development and fellowship applicants must arrange for resubmission of the three reference letters required for those programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure referees submit updated letters as part of the resubmission process so the application meets program-specific letter requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal-specific resubmission limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: After an unsuccessful submission and/or resubmission of a renewal application, your only option for a subsequent application is to submit as a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While you can submit a renewal resubmission application after an unsuccessful renewal application, you cannot submit a second renewal application following an unsuccessful renewal application—effectively limiting repeat renewal resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for award decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission applications follow the same timeline as other applications (~9 months to award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project start times and institutional commitments with the ~9-month review-to-award timeline in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission identification (A1 suffix)
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmission has a suffix in its application identification number, e.g., A1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct application type and identifier when submitting and tracking the application.
